chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabii, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who married a woman and stayed with her for some days, unable to have intercourse with her, except that he had seen from her that which is forbidden to others (i.e., private parts), then he divorced her. Is it permissible for him to marry her daughter? He said: 'Is it permissible for him, given that he had seen from her mother that which he saw?'

These two narrations are construed as indicating dislike (karahah) rather than prohibition (hazr), because that which necessitates prohibition is what we mentioned previously regarding consummation (muwaqah), according to what the apparent meaning of the Quran indicates. And it is not permissible for a man to marry the woman upon whom his father contracted marriage, in all cases.
Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not marry those women whom your fathers married.'

Thus, by the apparent meaning of the wording, it prohibits the marriage of what the fathers married. And 'marriage' (nikah) is an expression for the contract (aqd) in Islamic jurisprudence. And what confirms what we mentioned is what was narrated:

key_terms.اَلْكَرَاهِيَة: Dislike (a legal status between permissibility and prohibition)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry his ex-wife's daughter if he divorced her before consummation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi distinguishes between mere observation and consummation to determine whether the prohibition is absolute or merely disliked, clarifying that the Quranic verse 'do not marry what your fathers married' refers to the validity of the marriage contract (aqd) rather than sexual intercourse alone. This interpretation aligns with the Shia juristic view that the father's marriage bond creates a barrier for the son regardless of consummation, while the son's own marriage to the mother does not automatically prohibit him from marrying her daughter unless specific conditions of consummation are met.
